precepts.text: For where envying and strife is, there is confusion and every evil work. The word of God is pure and there is no variableness in it; there should be no confusion in what is being said. The confusion is that wisdom which descendeth not from above, but is earthly, sensual, devilish: it is deceiving you. Then you wonder why good things are withheld from you and why you cannot move forward.
precepts.point: Every captain who has sat in counsel knows the look: you tell a person what they are doing wrong, and they squint, get confused, and repeat back the very thing you just said. It is the battle in the mind at that moment; right is coming in, and wrong is warring against it.

note.label: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.why:
James 4:1 asks, “From whence come wars and fightings among you?” When you are told something you are doing wrong and something in you is adverse to correction, right is coming in and wrong is warring against it. Captains who have sat in counsel know the look: you tell somebody they don't listen, and they squint like they are confused and repeat back what you just said. It ain't their sight that went bad. It is the battle in the mind, manifesting in the face.

James shows where that confusion comes from: “For where envying and strife is, there is confusion and every evil work.” The word of God is pure; there is no variableness in it, and there should be no confusion in what is being said. If you were sincere, you would say, show me the lie, help me understand, maybe I am in error. Instead you are confused, because you are warring with what is right and don't want to accept it. You have strife in your heart.

“This wisdom descendeth not from above, but is earthly, sensual, devilish.” It is deceiving you, the same deceiving we read in chapter one.

Then you wonder why good things are withheld from you and why you can't move forward. You are a liar, a thief, a murderer, an adulterer, it is being identified to you, and you cannot reason with yourself. You are struggling with yourself, and that is the war in your members.

precepts.text: For where envying and strife is, there is confusion and every evil work. Now Cain did not know right from wrong; he slew his brother. Confusion is Satan's playground; that is why his children throw all types of confusion into the media wherever they go, because every evil work is behind that cloud of confusion.
precepts.point: And Cain talked with Abel his brother: this is the deception. He acted like his friend, talked with him over a period of time, and lured him out to the field. And when they were in the field, Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him. That is the spirit you are rolling in when you move with that bitter spirit; in that wrath you will slay a brother, or in that bitterness you might betray a brother.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.why:
“For where envying and strife is, there is confusion and every evil work.” Genesis 4 is an account of envying and strife. Cain was not doing right, he saw Abel doing right, and that built envy, the same spirit that shows up later between Esau and Jacob. It was there from the beginning.

Then comes confusion. All of a sudden Cain did not know right from wrong, and every evil work followed: he slew his brother. When you are confused, saying, I do not know where this is coming from, every evil work will be the result.

Confusion is Satan's playground. Satan loves us operating in confusion. That is why his children throw every kind of confusion into the media and everywhere they go, and why leaders of other nations have said they do not want that American media in their countries. They know every evil work hides behind that cloud of confusion.

precepts.text: That is why the scriptures say the greater condemnation: if you aspire to leadership, make sure your spirit is right, because if you fold when you are tried, you are accountable for all the souls that fold right along with you.
precepts.point: Nehemiah shows the right spirit. In the Persian captivity he had liberty from the king to rebuild the walls of Jerusalem, and the enemies Sanballat, Tobiah, and Geshem plotted to scare him off the work. A hired man urged him to hide in the temple because they were coming to slay him, and Nehemiah refused; operating in the spirit of fear is sin according to the scripture.

note.label: 1 Samuel 13: Make Not Haste in Time of Trouble

precepts.why:
“My brethren, be not many masters, knowing that we shall receive the greater condemnation.” That is why the scriptures say the greater condemnation.

If you aspire to leadership, make sure your spirit is right, because if you fold when you are tried, you are accountable for all the souls that fold right along with you.

precepts.text: He that offends not in word is a perfect man, able to bridle the whole body; read this chapter if you struggle with a foul mouth or talking back.
precepts.point: The Most High has proved and visited him and found nothing; David is purposed that his mouth shall not transgress.

note.label: Psalm 17: Keep Me as the Apple of the Eye

precepts.why:
“I am purposed that my mouth shall not transgress.” “For in many things we offend all. If any man offend not in word, the same is a perfect man, and able also to bridle the whole body.” He that offends not in word is a perfect man, able to bridle the whole body. David prays from real and not fake lips, a prayer “that goeth not out of feigned lips”, feigned meaning fake, and he is purposed that his mouth shall not transgress.

If you struggle with a foul mouth or talking back, read this chapter of James.

precepts.text: Where envying and strife is, there is confusion and every evil work.
precepts.point: Evil begins in the thoughts of the mind, so the strife the fool starts flows from an evil heart.

note.label: Proverbs 17: Trials That Refine and the Weight of Words

precepts.why:
“The beginning of strife is as when one letteth out water: therefore leave off contention, before it be meddled with.” Leave it off before it starts, because “where envying and strife is, there is confusion and every evil work.”

Strife let out is like water let out: once it is meddled with, confusion and every evil work follow. That is why contention is left off at its beginning.

precepts.text: Out of the same mouth proceed blessing and cursing; these things ought not so to be.
precepts.point: A man that has friends must show himself friendly, and there is a friend that sticks closer than a brother.

note.label: Proverbs 18: The Power of the Tongue and Righteous Judgment

precepts.why:
“Death and life are in the power of the tongue: and they that love it shall eat the fruit thereof.” The things you say can build someone up or tear them down, and those that love the tongue eat its fruit, whichever fruit it is.

James puts his finger on the trouble: “Out of the same mouth proceedeth blessing and cursing. My brethren, these things ought not so to be.” The same tongue that holds life and death lets out both, blessing one moment and cursing the next. That is not how it ought to be among brethren.

So the power of the tongue is a charge to keep it: a man's belly is filled with the fruit of his own mouth, and the mouth that blesses and curses in the same breath is eating the wrong fruit.
